entities.summary: Liu Yiqing (b. 403 CE, Xuzhou) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, active in Xuzhou. Known in the fields of journalists & chroniclers. His significance lies in his role as a key figure in the Jin dynasty's administration, overseeing the compilation of the 'Spring and Autumn Annals,' a comprehensive historical record of China's Warring States period. This monumental work provided a unified narrative of Chinese history, shaping the nation's collective memory and influencing the development of historiography for centuries to come. Liu's contributions also extend to his service as a military commander and diplomat, playing a crucial role in the Jin dynasty's expansion and interactions with neighboring states. His legacy as a chronicler and statesman has endured, with his works continuing to be studied and referenced by scholars and historians today.
